messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multilevel Analysis
parts: I am going to do a one-level SEM, just looking at if the gender (male or female) would also have some contributions to the dependent variable. So I just wonder if Lavaan can do this one level, or just how to code this path in the lavann package?

You can create a dummy code (e.g., 1 = female, 0 = male) to represent gender, then include it as a predictor in your model.  See the tutorial for how to specify regression paths:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax1.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multilevel Analysis
parts: You can build a model however you think is appropriate, e.g., based on substantive theory and past research if you are doing confirmatory research, or progressively using data-driven techniques if you are doing exploratory research. Regression textbooks typically have some discussion on model building.  If you have actual lavaan questions or problems, you can post your syntax to this group for help.  But because you say you aren't running a multilevel model (apparently estimating fixed effects of "subject" instead of random effects, for whatever reason), it would be more appropriate to post your questions about lavaan syntax in a new thread instead of replying to this one.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
